subject: Re: Request — batch inference completion windows & contract amendment
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightmetric.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightmetric.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Batch job completions outside contracted window

Kimberly —

We observed multiple nights last week where our nightly bulk inference jobs (approx. 1.8M records/day) finished well outside the 6-hour completion window outlined in our onboarding notes. The outcome: downstream reporting jobs missed SLA and a few customer alerts were delayed.

Quick context: jobs are kicked off at 01:00 PT, the observed completion spread was between 10:00–14:00 PT on 2027-05-27 and again 2027-05-29. We attached representative logs and timestamps.

Ask: would Redwood consider a one-time SLA remediation (credit or amendment) and a written commitment on maximum async completion window plus recommended retry/idempotency guidance so our infra team can adapt? We’re close to renewing and want to avoid recurring incidents.

Thanks —
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform, BrightMetric Analytics
attachments: customer_batch_log_snippets.zip

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightmetric.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightmetric.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Batch job completions outside contracted window

Hi Jordan —

Really sorry for the disruption and thanks for the clear logs. We take batch completion guarantees seriously. I’ve looped in Rishi (Account lead) and Dev (inference infra) so we can propose a remediation and a concrete operational amendment.

Immediate next steps:
- Internal postmortem: we’ll correlate job duration with cluster utilization and topology for the reported dates (Rishi/Dev)
- Draft amendment: propose explicit completion window language for async bulk jobs (e.g., 95th percentile completion within X hours) and agreed remedies (credit or service extension)
- Technical guidance: provide a short doc on safe retry patterns and idempotency keys to mitigate duplicates when customers requeue (Dev)

I’ll send a draft amendment and guidance by next week. In the meantime, can you confirm whether BrightMetric uses client-side retries today and whether you can accept an idempotency key per job batch?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Manager, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightmetric.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Batch job completions outside contracted window — technical remediation proposal

On Wed, Jun 2, 2027 at 10:03 AM kimberly_park wrote:
> I’ll send a draft amendment and guidance by next week. In the meantime, can you confirm whether BrightMetric uses client-side retries today and whether you can accept an idempotency key per job batch?

Quick technical note from infra: we investigated preliminary telemetry for the timestamps Jordan attached. Two things likely compounded the long tail: a) diurnal hardware load spikes that pushed batches into lower-priority pools, and b) a concurrency misconfiguration in BrightMetric’s orchestrator that retried a subset of failed shards aggressively (causing amplification).

Proposed short-term mitigations (to include in guidance doc):
- Completion window definition: we propose a contractual 95th percentile completion target of 6 hours for nightly bulk jobs up to 2M records, with a scalability clause for larger sizes.
- Retry policy: recommend exponential backoff with capped attempts (max 3) and jitter; require client-supplied idempotency-key at the batch level to make retries safe.
- Idempotency semantics: server-side dedupe window of 72 hours for idempotency-key values, with best-effort at 7 days for audit linking.
- Safe fallback: if job duration exceeds 8 hours (predicted by runtime estimator), auto-notify client and offer partial results streaming so critical consumers can begin processing.

I’ll draft an \"async-retry-spec.md\" with concrete headers, sample backoff config, and code snippets for typical orchestrators.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightmetric.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightmetric.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Draft amendment: async job completion window and remedies (v1)

Jordan / Priya —

Thank you for your patience. Attached is our proposed amendment to the Master Services Agreement (MSA) to add explicit language for bulk/async job completion windows and remedies. Highlights:

- Service objective: for nightly bulk inference jobs <= 2M records, Redwood will target 95th percentile completion <= 6 hours when jobs are submitted according to the agreed start window.
- Remedies: if Redwood fails the objective for two or more calendar days in a 30-day period, customer can request a credit up to 5% of monthly service fees for that period OR an extension of equivalent compute hours.
- Exceptional events: carveouts for force majeure or pre-announced maintenance.
- Operational addendum: includes the attached \"async-retry-spec.md\" and a summary of idempotency-key handling and dedupe windows.

Attachments: redwood_sla_amendment_v1.docx, async-retry-spec.md

Next steps we propose:
1) You review and flag any terms you want changed (credits vs. SLA service extension).
2) We schedule a 30-min call to walk the amendment and the idempotency pattern.
3) If accepted, we push the amendment through DocuSign (link included).

Kimberly will coordinate the call — are you available next week (Jun 14–16)?

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightmetric.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightmetric.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft amendment: async job completion window and remedies (v1)

Rishi/Kim —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. The amendment looks reasonable overall. Two small asks before we sign:
1) Can the credit remedy be expanded to 7% for cases where the 95th percentile breach affects customer-facing alerts (we can provide examples)?
2) Can you include a short clause that requires Redwood to provide a per-incident post-incident timeline and root cause write-up within 5 business days for any SLA breach?

We can do the 30-min walkthrough on Thu Jun 17 at 10:00 PT — will that work for your team? If we agree on the two tweaks above, I’ll sign via DocuSign after the call.

Thanks —
Jordan
Head of Platform, BrightMetric Analytics
